who-this-is-for.text: A reviewer who wants to play a naming claim in the docs, not read a proposed walkthrough.

what-you-can-do.text: Choose the labelled first-release naming profile, claim alice, queue a competing claim, and fold each request. The first valid absent-key fold succeeds; the duplicate is refused because the key is occupied.

what-you-see-when-it-is-refused.text: Every refusal names its intended condition. Approval never occupies a spelling. Uniqueness is decided only when a certified Insert folds.

first-release-naming-profile.text: The playable surface is an explicit naming profile labelled as an unaccepted candidate. Certification proves allowed construction only. The spelling alice is a frozen demo fixture.

registry-uniqueness-at-fold.text: The state diagram shows absent, pending, and active. The first valid fold of an absent key becomes active. A competing fold is refused.

application-fixture-fields.text: The initial application record has an optional payment destination, a control address, a next-control commitment, and a fixed retirement quorum. This slice stores them as structure only.

generic-profile-stays-generic.text: A separate generic profile remains labelled generic and can still delete. It cannot silently become the naming profile.

limits-of-this-slice.text: Natural numbers, no ledger execution, and no maintenance, recovery, retirement, or consumer scenarios. Naming theorems are a new inventory. The preview states the candidate is unaccepted.
